Laundry Service SaiGon
Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam1 contribution

It's really good
Apr 2026 • Couples
Honest, no-frills phở with rich, well-balanced broth — my go-to spot when I want something authentic without the tourist markup. The bò viên is excellent and they have plenty of options for both beef and chicken phở.

What I appreciate:
- Open from early morning, perfect for breakfast
- English menu available
- Plenty of fresh herbs and limes on the table
- Reasonable prices for District 3 (around 90-120K VND/bowl)

Service can be brisk during peak hours (locals lunch crowd) but the quality stays consistent. Skip the trendy phở chains and come here if you want the real deal.

Tip: order it "đặc biệt" (special) for all the meat varieties, or ask for "tái" if you want rare beef cooked by the broth.

Pho, Banh Quay, Pateso… and Pure Saigon Chaos in the Best Way
Oct 2025 • Couples
Pho Hoa Pasteur is one of Saigon’s great pho institutions, the kind of place where the line between “restaurant” and “controlled chaos” disappears in the best possible way. It sits proudly on Pasteur, easy to find, impossible to forget, and always humming with energy. If Pho Minh is quiet wisdom, Pho Hoa is the city’s heartbeat.

The atmosphere hits you first. Tables packed, bowls landing faster than you can blink, staff moving with the speed and precision of a pit crew. It’s loud, busy, and alive — exactly the sort of place Anthony Bourdain would call “proper eating.”

And then there’s the food. Pho Hoa’s broth is lighter, brighter, and more herb-forward than some of Saigon’s old-guard shops. It’s clean and fragrant, built for freshness rather than heaviness. The noodles come out perfectly cooked, the beef tender and generous, and the herb basket is practically overflowing.

But what sets Pho Hoa apart is the glorious side-dish setup that fills every table. You don’t just get pho — you get an entire supporting cast. There are banh quay, those irresistible fried dough sticks perfect for dunking into hot broth. Banh pateso, flaky puff pastries filled with savoury meat, sit alongside piles of fried tofu, spring rolls, and other small bites designed to tempt you into ordering more than you planned. It feels like a feast even when you only walked in for one bowl.

Service is lightning fast. You sit, you order, and within minutes your bowl is steaming in front of you. No fuss, no ceremony — just efficient, confident execution from a team that’s been doing this for decades.

The value is excellent. For such an iconic, high-volume spot, the pricing is still incredibly reasonable. With the side dishes on the table, you can tailor your meal to exactly how hungry you are… or how hungry the restaurant convinces you to be.

Wait times look intimidating from the street, but don’t be fooled. This place moves people through with remarkable speed. Even at peak times, you’ll be seated before you’ve had a chance to reconsider.

Overall, Pho Hoa Pasteur is a must-visit. It’s loud, fast, full of life, and utterly delicious. A pho experience that feels quintessentially Saigon — chaotic, generous, and unforgettable.

Insider tip:
Go early. It gets busy fast. Order the Pho Dac Biet and grab banh quay or pateso from the table — both perfect with the broth. Bring cash.
